fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Myth as the Dream of a Culture", "body": "Loralee Scaife builds her approach on the Jung and Campbell idea that myth is to a culture what dreams are to the individual, and she reads the Lord of the Rings films through amplification, a Jungian dream technique that gathers the connotations of a symbol. Applied to a meme that turns the Statue of Liberty into the Eye of Sauron, it surfaces Prometheus carrying his torch and Galadriel holding her light. The talk frames Prometheus bringing fire home to his people against Sauron stealing it to wield power over others."}, {"title": "A Myth for Our Time and Its Ancient Roots", "body": "Loralee says she met Tolkien in December 2001, a few months after September 11, and was struck by how the story confronted evil. She argues the tale helps modern so-called men of the West reconnect with ancient roots, echoing Galadriel's line that much that once was is lost. Chance wonders aloud about America's transplanted mythology and, citing a researcher he is reading, floats the contested idea that some old buildings were found rather than built. In his solo outro Chance recommends an article, Tolkien at the End of Time, and speculates that Tolkien's command of ancient languages may have let him read a real takeover in old texts."}, {"title": "Saturn, Pluto, and the Shadow Cycle", "body": "Speaking as an astrologer, Loralee traces the 35 to 38 year Saturn and Pluto cycle, noting an opposition just weeks before September 11 and a conjunction in 2020, and she interprets both periods as moments when shadow and evil press into public view. Her practical point is that personal shadow work leaves less room for archetypal evil to take over a personality. She presents her reading of recent events as her own view of a fearful, manipulated population. The conversation adds a nineteen year lunar cycle linking 2001 and 2020, and the wordplay that Sauron sounds like Saturn, the planet with the ring."}, {"title": "The Ring as Circle, Torus, and Life Force", "body": "Unpacking the One Ring, Loralee starts with the circle, moves through the ouroboros, the zodiac and the zero, then into sacred geometry and the torus, which she describes as the structure behind everything from particles to galaxies. She argues that knowledge of the torus is kept from people and that this explains why forces of evil would crave the ring. Chance contributes a reading of ouroboros as the infinite emerging from nothingness, with the zero as the repressed feminine and shadow, and Loralee points to the six pointed star and caduceus in Arwen's jewel."}, {"title": "Evil as Anti-Life and the Weight of Kingship", "body": "Loralee observes that evil is live spelled backwards, a wordplay Chance says he points out all the time, and she describes evil as anti-life, something that cannot create and instead feeds on what others make. She finds it startling how naive most people are about evil. In her view, waiting for white hats or any outside savior is projection, because Gandalf refused the ring out of awareness of his own shadow, and the answer is personal responsibility and an inner king. Chance adds that evil works less through lies than through obscuring the truth, so people must reclaim ancestral knowledge."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Loralee Scaife is an astrologer who uses Jungian techniques to analyze mythology, using stories to map the collective unconscious. She's created a video series using The Lord of the Rings films and books as a mystical mythic lens through which we can better understand our troubled times. In our discussion on Tolkien's tales, we analyze the nature of evil and our responsibility to stand up as the good folk of the world, in defense of the Life Force itself.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension, we talk about Tolkien's cosmology, the universal creative purpose of tragedy, lies, and sorrow, the light and shadow of the King archetype, cymatics and the secrets of sound & light, ancestors living in our language, the Age of Aquarius, and the myth of Prometheus. A jam packed extension if there ever was one!

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Music of the Ainur and the Why of Evil", "body": "Loralee offers a short account of the cosmology in the Silmarillion, where the creator brings forth the Ainur as thoughts shaped into music and then kindles them with the flame imperishable. She links it to the standard scientific story that sound preceded light. Chance notes that Earth is an anagram of heart and discusses Melkor, the most powerful Ainur, whose dissonance opens the question of evil. Loralee suggests that a perfect life would produce no growth, and that cycles of order and chaos spiral toward greater complexity, an idea Chance echoes by asking whether truth needs lies."}, {"title": "Domination, Vampirism, and the Four Part King", "body": "Loralee traces Melkor and Sauron to jealousy, anger and fear, rooted in terror, rage and grief, which harden into a will to dominate. She calls it vampiric, since those who cannot create feed on others, and Chance adds that the more control they seize, the weaker they become. Using Robert Moore's work, Loralee then describes the king, warrior, magician and lover as a four part structure, illustrating the magician with Aragorn trusting Gandalf at Helm's Deep, while Chance adds that archetypes often reach us from outside before we carry them within."}, {"title": "Ancestry, Language, and Resonance", "body": "Chance asks what is lost by knowing only a few generations of ancestors, and Loralee calls it a terrible loss, citing Galadriel's line and the current interest in genealogy and genetics. Chance wonders whether chanting ancestors' names might draw their traits into one's field, and he says he has never seen anything convincing that memory lives in the brain, a view he offers as his own opinion. Loralee suggests Tolkien's deep study of ancient languages let him tap a coherent resonance carrying knowledge reaching back thousands of years."}, {"title": "Sovereignty, Small Groups, and the Fellowship", "body": "The conversation contrasts democracy with conscious kingship, proposing that monarchy is a symbol of individual sovereignty and that freedom means responsibility. Loralee argues that democracy works only among small, informed groups and predicts a breaking up into smaller tribes where leaders who have mastered their inner worlds arise. Chance agrees that care depends on knowing each other. They offer the Fellowship, with Gimli and Legolas overcoming old antagonism rather than projecting evil onto each other, as the model."}, {"title": "Prometheus, Aquarius, and the Hobbits", "body": "Loralee argues the Promethean archetype is a force of nature that rises when the life force is threatened, and she links it to the Jupiter and Saturn conjunction in Aquarius on the 2020 winter solstice, which she reads as a call to form fellowships. Chance argues that Prometheus, Venus, Lucifer and Galadriel share an archetype of light, insisting he is no Luciferian. Loralee closes with the view that evil destroys itself in the end, and the talk ends on the hobbits carrying the torch of goodness through small acts, with the Shire as the great mother's garden."}]

fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Myths that stick with us as a people are the expression of our collective psyche reflecting itself back to us.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "My approach in the beginning was based on Jung and Campbell's idea that myth is to a culture what dreams are to the individual.", "author": "Loralee Scaife", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/72d8aecf-5728-42c6-976e-427104fb9105/LORALEE-SCAIFE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There is certainly a prophetic quality to Lord of the Rings.", "author": "Loralee Scaife", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/72d8aecf-5728-42c6-976e-427104fb9105/LORALEE-SCAIFE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "What we have in America is a mythology that's been transplanted from another land onto this land.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If we as individuals are doing our own personal shadow work, then we're less likely to be leaving the door open for archetypal evil to creep in and essentially take over the personality.", "author": "Loralee Scaife", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/72d8aecf-5728-42c6-976e-427104fb9105/LORALEE-SCAIFE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Evil is live or live spelled backwards. There's a pretty powerful word play right there.", "author": "Loralee Scaife", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/72d8aecf-5728-42c6-976e-427104fb9105/LORALEE-SCAIFE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's an anti-life force in existence right now. And it is literally on the march because so many people simply will not even consider that there is evil.", "author": "Loralee Scaife", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/72d8aecf-5728-42c6-976e-427104fb9105/LORALEE-SCAIFE.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Even something that was made just for convenience and had no ill intent could weaken us in the long run by making us dependent on it.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
